entries.title: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line Shapefiles
entries.description: The Census Bureau's annual extracts of its MAF/TIGER geographic database: legal and statistical boundaries (states, counties, county subdivisions, places, tracts, block groups, blocks, congressional and legislative districts, ZCTAs, PUMAs and more), roads, rail, hydrography and landmarks, with the geographic codes that join to Census data. The standard boundary files behind US statistics.

coverage.temporal: 2007-present as shapefiles (2026 edition latest); ASCII TIGER/Line for 2006 and earlier

Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl; content read with headless Chromium). The page lists "Shapefile - 2007 to Present" and "TIGER/Line ASCII format - 2006 and earlier" and says "The core TIGER/Line Files and Shapefiles do not include demographic data, but they do contain geographic entity codes that can be linked to the Census Bureau’s demographic data". Latest: "2026 TIGER/Line Shapefiles ... All legal boundaries and names are as of January 1, 2026. The 2026 TIGER/Line Shapefiles were released on October 14, 2026", with Download, Web Interface and FTP Archive links.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: no data-specific licence statement was found. The public-domain status rests on the Census Bureau being a federal agency (17 U.S.C. §105), which is how other Census entries in this workspace record it. Not checked: the geodatabase and KML cartographic boundary products (a separate series), or the TIGERweb services.

entries.description: Pan-European land cover and land use inventory in 44 thematic classes, produced for reference years 1990, 2000, 2006, 2012 and 2018 with change layers between them, at a 25 ha minimum mapping unit. entries.title: Copernicus DEM (GLO-30, GLO-90 and EEA-10 Digital Elevation Model)
entries.description: Global digital surface model derived from the TanDEM-X mission (2011-2015), distributed by the European Space Agency under the EU Copernicus programme at 30 m and 90 m worldwide (GLO-30, GLO-90) and 10 m over 39 European countries (EEA-10). The most widely used open global elevation baseline after SRTM.
entries.publisher: European Space Agency (ESA), Copernicus Contributing Missions, via the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem

access.auth_note: Free Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem registration required; general public may download GLO-30 and GLO-90 only, EEA-10 download is limited to eligible users (public authorities, EU institutions, EU-funded research, etc.).

NUTS and LAU are the boundary sets that EU regional statistics are published against.

The page "基盤地図情報サイト" (last updated 2026-03-07) links to the download service and says "基盤地図情報をダウンロードする場合には、ダウンロードページでユーザ登録とログインが必要です" (registration and login are required to download). The download service (https://service.gsi.go.jp/kiban/) showed notices "2026-10-30 提供データを整備・更新しました（基本項目）" and "2026-07-31 ... （数値標高モデル）", and that the coordinate reference system changed from JGD2011 to JGD2024. GSI also offers a free viewer (FGDV) that exports to Shapefile.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: GSI's Content Terms of Use (https://www.gsi.go.jp/kikakuchousei/kikakuchousei40182.html, revised 令和7年11月20日) state "本サイトのコンテンツには特段の記載が無い限り公共データ利用規約（第1.0 版）（PDL1.0）が適用されています" (site content is under Public Data License v1.0 unless otherwise stated), with a source credit such as "出典：国土地理院ウェブサイト（当該ページのURL）" and a note when content is edited. The download service answered HTTP 200 to plain curl the same day.

entries.title: Natural Earth (public-domain small-scale world map data)
entries.description: Public-domain vector and raster world map data at 1:10m, 1:50m and 1:110m scales: country and first-level subdivision boundaries (including disputed-area treatments), populated places, coastlines, rivers, lakes, relief and other cultural and physical themes, generalised so that layers align. A de facto default for small-scale world and regional maps, made by volunteers rather than an official mapping agency.
entries.publisher: Natural Earth (volunteer project; primary authors Tom Patterson and Nathaniel Vaughn Kelso; supported by the North American Cartographic Information Society, NACIS)

recovery.notes: Recorded by scripts/capture_archives.py on 2026-11-04: a capture it requested from Save Page Now.

entries.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The home page says "Natural Earth is a public domain map dataset available at 1:10m, 1:50m, and 1:110 million scales" and that it "was built through a collaboration of many volunteers and is supported by NACIS (North American Cartographic Information Society)". The Downloads page offers "all vector themes as SHP (576 mb), SQLite (423 mb), or GeoPackage (436 mb)" and per-scale Cultural, Physical and Raster pages. Publisher honesty: this is a volunteer-made dataset, not an official or treaty body. jurisdiction.scope is set to international-ngo only because the schema has no better value. Its boundaries are cartographic generalisations, and its treatment of disputed borders reflects the project's editorial choices, not any government's position; prefer UN SALB, Eurostat GISCO or national agencies where official boundaries matter.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: Terms of Use (https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/) state "All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data found on this website are in the public domain" and "No permission is needed to use Natural Earth. Crediting the authors is unnecessary". The attribution recorded is the optional "long text" citation the page suggests. The page also quotes a Washington Post licence for some source data granted to Natural Earth. The site footer "© 2009 - 2026. Natural Earth. All rights reserved." refers to the website, not the data. Not checked: the current version number (the GitHub repo's latest-release API returned nothing), or the raster themes.

entries.license: proprietary-noncommercial (SALB Terms of Use 2021; copyright United Nations, no modification of geometry, non-commercial only)
entries.attribution: from SALB Data, United Nations, plus the contributing national authority named in the metadata
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium). The Data page lists "1 - 50 of 197 Member States" with each country's National Geospatial Information Authority, plus columns for Public Contacts, Historic Table and Geospatial Datasets. On the day checked, only some countries (e.g. Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Togo, Tonga) had a downloadable historic table (xlsx), and the Geospatial Datasets column read "None" for every country seen on pages 1 and 3, so boundary geometry may not be publicly downloadable from this page at present. The home page states the aim is geospatial data "for first and second level below national, at 1:1 million scale".
Licence checked 2026-11-01: Terms of Use PDF (https://salb.un.org/sites/default/files/wysiwyg_uploads/docs_uploads/TermsOfUseSALB2021.pdf, linked from the Methodology page; curl got 403, fetched via a browser session) states "Copyright of the SALB Data (including all codes, historical tables, and geospatial data) is vested in the United Nations", "Users are prohibited from changing the geometry or content of the SALB Data without consent of the Contributor", and "The SALB Data may be used for only non-commercial purposes." Derived products must include the phrase "from SALB Data, United Nations". This is a data-specific licence and is NOT an open licence. Not checked: geometry formats, per-country vintages, or whether a separate UN geoportal distributes the boundaries.

entries.title: USGS Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)
entries.description: The Federal and national standard gazetteer of US geographic names, maintained by the USGS for the U.S. Board on Geographic Names: the official name, feature class, location and variant names of physical and cultural features in the United States, its territories and Antarctica (excluding roads and highways). The authoritative source for US place-name spelling and feature IDs.
entries.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, for the U.S. Board on Geographic Names

coverage.spatial: United States, territories, associated areas, and Antarctica
coverage.temporal: current and historical feature names (static legacy archive last updated August 2021)

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work; USGS Copyrights and Credits policy)
entries.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, Geographic Names Information System (GNIS)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 to curl with a browser User-Agent; a plain curl User-Agent got 403 and headless Chromium got a CloudFront 403 page on usgs.gov. The page calls GNIS "The Federal and national standard for geographic nomenclature" and links domestic and Antarctic name search tools, a GNIS REST ArcGIS service and data downloads. It says GNIS holds "the Federally recognized name of each feature" for physical and cultural features "but not including roads and highways". The Download GNIS Data page (https://www.usgs.gov/us-board-on-geographic-names/download-gnis-data, HTTP 200) states "Data products are refreshed every other month", offers "pipe-delimited text (TXT) files" plus "file geodatabase [GDB] and GeoPackage [GPKG]", downloaded through The National Map Downloader, and notes an Archive file of "Static legacy domestic and Antarctica names data last updated August 2021".
Licence checked 2026-11-01: USGS Copyrights and Credits (https://www.usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits) states "USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain". This is an agency-wide data policy. Cadence is recorded as irregular although the download page says products are refreshed every other month (no matching schema value). Foreign names are not in GNIS; see nga-geonet-names-server. Not checked: the REST service or the file contents.

entries.title: USGS The National Map (3DEP elevation, hydrography, boundaries and topographic base data)
entries.description: The USGS National Geospatial Program's suite of nationally consistent base geospatial layers for the United States: 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) lidar and DEMs, hydrography (National Hydrography Dataset and its 3D Hydrography Program successor), boundaries, transportation, structures, geographic names, land cover and orthoimagery, plus US Topo and historical topographic maps, delivered through the TNM Downloader and web services.
entries.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program

coverage.temporal: varies by layer (current base data plus historical topographic maps)

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work; USGS Copyrights and Credits policy)
entries.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, The National Map
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 to curl with a browser User-Agent; a plain curl User-Agent got 403, and headless Chromium got a CloudFront "403 ERROR The request could not be satisfied" page, so usgs.gov is sensitive to client type. The page says "The National Map is a suite of products, services, and applications that provide access to base geospatial information representing the topography, natural landscape, and built environment of the United States and its territories" and that it "supports digital and print versions of topographic maps, data download, web map services, and online viewing". The program menu lists 3D Elevation Program, 3D Hydrography Program, Topographic Maps and the U.S. Board on Geographic Names. The TNM Downloader (https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/) answered HTTP 200 to curl.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: USGS Copyrights and Credits (https://www.usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits) states "USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain", with the caveat that some non-USGS material is copyrighted and marked. This is an agency-wide data policy. Partner-contributed layers in TNM may carry their own terms. Not checked: individual layer formats, the TNM Access API, and whether the National Hydrography Dataset is still offered alongside 3DHP. Format is left empty. Geographic names are catalogued separately as usgs-gnis.
